reviews.why: No checkpoint fell due this week -- the next, the ICSG's October statistics, is not due until November 10 -- and no new Escondida-specific news emerged: the October 20 operational review and the October 14 labor settlement are now a week old. Copper continued drifting lower alongside a broad risk-off week across equities and commodities (the Fed held rates on October 28 by a 10-2 vote), trading near $6.45/lb on October 30, essentially flat from $6.47/lb a week earlier, still well above the $6.15 kill level, and no closer to the September record the variant needs. The regulatory delay central to the thesis has still not surfaced.

no_new_call_note: A scan across commodities, crypto and stocks this week turned up nothing both new and confirmed by more than one independent source that the market has not already priced: a Fed decision to hold rates, a continued slide in silver after its well-publicized reversal, broad AI-spending-driven weakness in megacap tech and chip names, and the sixteen pending crypto ETF decisions carried over from last week are each already reported and already reflected in price, so no new call opens this week.
